newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S DOBREV SAYS PRESIDENT COULD NAME CABINET.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S DOBREV SAYS PRESIDENT COULD NAME CABINET.

text.p: Bulgarian Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev, the ruling Socialists' nominee for premier, proposed on Friday that President Petar Stoyanov should appoint a coalition government to bring the country out of crisis.
Dobrev said he would be willing to give up his mandate to form a government for the sake of consensus between warring political factions.
"I think the country now needs a constitutional government on a very wide political base," Dobrev told Reuters in an interview.

"I don't mind if it is formed under the leadership of the president as I highly respect the president's efforts to find a way out of the crisis," he said. "I am ready to return my mandate if such a government is formed."
Stoyanov, returning from a visit to Brussels on Friday, renewed his call for immediate elections and said Dobrev should give up the mandate.

The Socialists were elected in December 1994 and formally have nearly two years of their term left, but protesters have taken to the streets nationwide for 26 consecutive days to demand immediate elections.
